claims.text: Nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits negligible irradiation hardening.
Nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 undergoes radiation-induced precipitation under fusion-relevant energetic-particle irradiation.
The proposed intervention is addition of approximately 0.5 at.% Hf to W38Ta36Cr15V11 during processing.
Hf will preferentially segregate to grain boundaries.
Hf will preferentially segregate to radiation-induced defect clusters.
Segregated Hf will cause grain boundaries and defect clusters to act as enhanced defect sinks.
Hf segregation will reduce the local supersaturation of mobile irradiation-induced species.
Reduced local supersaturation of mobile species will limit precipitate nucleation.
Reduced local supersaturation of mobile species will limit precipitate growth.
At approximately 8 dpa and 300–500°C, the Hf-doped alloy will have a lower radiation-induced precipitate density than the unmodified alloy.
At approximately 8 dpa and 300–500°C, the Hf-doped alloy will have smaller radiation-induced precipitates than the unmodified alloy.
The Hf-doped alloy will retain or slightly improve the negligible irradiation-hardening behavior of the unmodified alloy.
The proposed mechanism will preserve microstructural stability.
The hypothesis is intended to apply up to approximately 8 dpa at 300–500°C.
Behavior outside approximately 8 dpa or outside 300–500°C is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome permits merely retaining the baseline's negligible hardening, but the falsification rule says that no improvement in hardening falsifies the hypothesis. Thus an outcome explicitly allowed by the prediction would also trigger falsification.
